title: Proof-of-Workout Fraud Shield for Fitness Incentives
one_liner: A verification API that scores whether a gym visit or workout really happened, priced per verified event.
customer: Administrators of pay-per-visit fitness benefits (regional Medicare Advantage plans, employer stipend platforms), movement-reward and fitness-betting apps.
problem: Chain: Medicare Advantage plans are trimming fitness benefits (93 percent offered one in 2026 versus 95 percent in 2025, more cuts expected) and payers and employers shift toward pay-per-verified-visit and reward models (one employer wellness network lists over 20,000 employer partners), so money follows check-ins and step counts. Fraud (shared QR codes, spoofed steps, ghost visits, inflated gym counts) becomes the margin killer and nobody sells fraud scoring built for fitness.
solution: An SDK and API combining phone attestation, gym BLE or Wi-Fi beacons, wearable heart-rate and motion consistency, GPS and barometer, and device-sharing graphs into an authenticity score with an audit trail, ring detection and a dispute workflow for gyms.
why_now: Benefit cuts push payers to pay-per-use, wearable aggregator APIs make cross-signal checks cheap, and mobile attestation is mature; HIPRA-style consent rules make audit trails a requirement.
revenue_model: $0.05-0.20 per verified event with a $2-5k monthly minimum, plus a gain share on recovered fraud.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is a labeled fraud dataset: once you process millions of visits you can sell audits to payers, and because you are neutral infrastructure you compete with no wearable or gym software vendor.
first_30_days: Find 2-3 reward or betting apps or one regional benefit administrator, run their last 90 days of check-ins through a prototype scorer, quantify suspected fraud, and charge $5-10k for the audit before integrating.

title: Incretin-in-a-Drop Assay for Life Underwriting
one_liner: A dried-blood-spot or oral-fluid lab test that tells insurers whether an applicant is actually on semaglutide, tirzepatide, orforglipron or retatrutide.
customer: Life and disability insurers, reinsurers, MGAs and paramedical exam vendors, with bariatric programs, trial sponsors and outcome-based employer programs as follow-on buyers.
problem: Cash-pay and direct-ship fills (LillyDirect, NovoCare, telehealth-partner pharmacies, compounders, gray market) are only partly visible in claims-based Rx histories, so BMI looks 'preferred' while drug-supported. Stopping the drug means rebound and adverse selection. Gray-market retatrutide is invisible by design.
solution: A validated LC-MS/MS panel (semaglutide, tirzepatide, orforglipron, cagrilintide, retatrutide) run by a partner CLIA lab as an add-on to the paramedical exam, returning 'on-board, recent use or none'. Later expansions to pre-op verification, adherence-verified outcome contracts and a consumer 'proof of adherence' report.
why_now: Published LC-MS/MS methods for semaglutide and tirzepatide matured in 2026, the FDA's LDT rule was vacated in 2025, and cash-pay pill volume exploded in 2026 (Wegovy pill >2M scripts).
revenue_model: $25-45 per test as an underwriting add-on, volume tiers for carriers, and later $79 consumer or clinician tests.
non_obvious_insight: This is the first mass-market chronic drug that bypasses the industry's data plumbing. Underwriters will pay for direct measurement over questionnaires because the cost of a wrong mortality class is far above $35.
first_30_days: Ask two Rx-history vendors what share of DTC fills they see. Contract a CLIA tox lab to validate an assay from published methods. Pitch 10 MGAs and reinsurer innovation teams, and run a paid 200-sample blinded pilot with one friendly insurer, with consent and state unfair-discrimination rules reviewed by counsel.

title: Retired Operators as Fractional Rural Water Chiefs
one_liner: A cooperative of retired licensed water operators, each serving as the certified 'operator in responsible charge' for several tiny water systems remotely plus monthly visits, while converting their tacit knowledge into digital manuals.
customer: Small community water systems under about 3,300 people (councils, water districts, mobile-home park owners, county utilities). State rural water associations and engineering firms refer them. Each pays a $2.5-5k/month retainer.
problem: About a third of the water workforce is eligible to retire within a decade, and tiny systems cannot compete for certified operators. No software fixes 'nobody with a license answers the phone at 2 a.m.' PFAS initial monitoring is due in 2027, the lead action level tightens to 0.010 mg/L on Nov 1, 2027, and nitrate hits small farm-belt systems hardest. Meanwhile 60-72-year-old operators want part-time income, autonomy and purpose.
solution: Recruit retirees holding Grade 2-4 certifications. Each covers 3-5 systems using remote SCADA and camera access, a compliance calendar (sampling, PFAS monitoring, lead-inventory reporting, consumer confidence reports) and a shared on-call rotation inside the co-op. Every operator records an 'exit interview' that becomes site-specific SOPs (which valve sticks, which well drops in August). A young apprentice is attached to each cluster so succession is built in. The co-op keeps 25-30%.
why_now: 2027 PFAS and lead-rule deadlines are close, and $7.2B of FY2026 State Revolving Fund money flows to systems that must show capable operations. Boomer retirements are peaking. Federal technical capacity is shrinking (EPA's research office was eliminated in 2026), and small systems are left on their own.
revenue_model: $2.5-5k per system per month retainer, of which the co-op keeps 25-30% and the operator earns roughly $30-50k a year part-time. One-off compliance projects (PFAS sampling programs, lead service line inventories) add $5-20k each.
non_obvious_insight: Tiny systems do not need 'AI SCADA'. They need one accountable licensed human, and the only growing supply of licensed operators is retirees. Many states let one certified operator be in responsible charge of several small systems (rules vary by state and need checking). The retiree's tacit local knowledge is the real asset being lost.
first_30_days: Partner with the state Rural Water Association and get the drinking-water program's list of systems with operator-certification violations. Recruit 8 retired operators through the association newsletter and conference. Sign 3 systems on 90-day trial retainers.

title: Paid Farm Residencies That Recruit Successors
one_liner: Multi-week hospitality-designed farm stays that let heir-less owners audition would-be farmers, monetising the stay and taking a success fee if a lease-to-own follows.
customer: Owners aged 65+ of orchards, vineyards, dairies and livestock farms with no heir, plus career-changing or remote-working would-be farmers with capital who pay for the residency. Farm Credit lenders and estate lawyers are referral partners.
problem: About one-third of US farmers have no obvious heir, and only about 1 in 4 has a formal succession plan. Over 60% of farmland may change hands in 10-15 years, much of it through estates that listing sites never see. Existing matching programs are listing databases, so skill and personal fit stay unresolved until people actually work together, and farm incomes are squeezed by input costs.
solution: Run 2-4 week residencies at $3K-$6K per guest with lodging, meals, remote-work setup (Starlink and a desk), and structured farm-management workshops on finances, equipment and land tenure. A shortlisted guest can take a paid trial season as a W-2 employee. Provide lender introductions (beginning-farmer loans) and lease-to-own and Buy-Protect-Sell templates, and take a success fee at transition. Winter orchard and vineyard pruning gives a bookable season within six months.
why_now: Remote work and nomad visas created the first cohort able to relocate to a farm without quitting a job. Bankruptcies up 19% and a fourth straight year of row-crop losses are pushing owners to plan exits, and the 'invisible transfer' wave means estates, not listings, decide who gets land. AI-assistant booking now lets tiny hosts sell stays directly.
revenue_model: Guest fees of $3K-$6K. A $750 farmer onboarding fee. A success fee of $15K-$25K or 1-2% of land or lease value at transition.
non_obvious_insight: Successors are not found in databases but in the third week of living together, so hospitality is the screening technology. The stay revenue pays the retiring farmer to audition candidates instead of paying a broker, and the trust built also unlocks the seller-financing that beginning farmers usually lack.
first_30_days: Recruit 6 specialty farms with owners aged 65+ in the Hudson Valley, Vermont, the Willamette Valley and Michigan. Open applications through career-change and nomad newsletters, and pre-sell 20 winter-pruning residencies for Dec-Mar.

title: Pay-on-Pass: Inspections Trigger Sub Payments
one_liner: Same-day payment to framers and foundation crews the moment the city inspection clears, financed against the builder's draw.
customer: Small private builders (20-300 homes a year) and their framing, foundation, plumbing and electrical subs, with a community lender or credit line as funding partner.
problem: Cities adopt AI plan review, filings surge (Honolulu applications +34% but permits issued +5%, backlog 9,252), and the bottleneck moves to post-permit inspections. Subs wait for the pass, then wait for payment: one in five subs waits 60+ days and GCs are 4x more likely than subs to be paid within 30 days. Crews are already vanishing, so slow payers lose them.
solution: A payment rail keyed to a third-party-verified milestone: inspection status pulled from municipal portals or a photo of the green tag. The sub is paid within 24 hours from a revolving credit facility, repaid from the builder's draw within 30 days. Builders also get a crew reliability ranking and inspection-queue analytics by jurisdiction and inspector, with photo pre-checks to raise first-time pass rates.
why_now: AI permitting is deploying now (Honolulu, Denver's $4.6M contract), shifting the constraint downstream. Immigration enforcement makes verified crews scarce, so pay speed has become a recruiting tool. Completions are down 27.1%.
revenue_model: 1.5-2.5% of released payments, paid by the builder for speed and crew retention, with an optional sub-paid instant-pay discount. Spread on credit line usage.
non_obvious_insight: The inspection pass is the only moment in construction that is third-party verified, timestamped and dispute-proof, which makes it the ideal payment trigger and collateral. Nobody uses it because the data sits in thousands of scattered municipal portals, but one builder in one metro needs only three or four.
first_30_days: Pick one metro and its three permit portals. Pilot with 3 builders and their 5 framing and foundation subs. Open a $100-200K line with a friendly community lender. Verify passes by hand and pay by ACH.

title: Origin Assay: Forensic Testing of Metal Melt Origin
one_liner: A lab test that says where steel or aluminum was actually melted, so US-melt claims stop resting on paperwork alone.
customer: Importers and fabricators claiming the 10% US-melt rate, steel service centers selling premium 'US-melt' stock, customs counsel and insurers defending CBP audits, and buyers with domestic-metal requirements.
problem: Section 232 rates now depend on melt or smelt origin: 10% with US-melted metal against 25-50%. The certificate is worth thousands of dollars per ton, mill test reports can be relabeled or forged, and CBP is prioritizing origin verification and AD/CVD evasion. No independent test exists.
solution: Build a reference library by buying coupons from about 100 mills worldwide. Measure trace-element, inclusion and slag chemistry, and isotopic signatures (LIBS, ICP-MS, SEM-EDS). Train a classifier to give origin probability. First product is a mail-in Origin Assay with a confidence-scored report and sampling protocol built for audits. Handheld screening is a later roadmap. Classifier accuracy is the central risk, so start with one narrow discrimination, such as US EAF versus Chinese plate for one grade.
why_now: The 2026 tiers turn a chemistry fact into a financial asset. Cheaper mass spectrometry and machine learning make library-based classification plausible, and academic provenance work exists but no commercial library does (verify).
revenue_model: $300-900 per sample. $25-100k annual audit programs for service centers. Insurer verification programs. Later, handheld subscriptions.
non_obvious_insight: Duty policy turned melt origin into money, and paper certificates invite cheating, so the arbitrage is proof. Scrap-based EAF steel carries a fingerprint of tramp elements and alloy history that makes origin partly knowable.
first_30_days: Interview three service centers and three customs counsel. Buy or borrow about 40 heats of known origin (A36 and 304). Use a university ICP-MS lab to test discriminating power on two grades. Sell a $5k pilot verification of 10 suspicious heats.

title: Dispute Escrow for Agent Payments on Pix/UPI
one_liner: A neutral hold-and-evidence layer that gives agent-initiated Pix and UPI payments the dispute protection cards have and push rails never did.
customer: Brazilian WhatsApp-commerce, bill-pay and shopping-agent startups and their sponsoring payment institutions, plus Indian UPI apps building agentic checkout. Marketplaces and merchants who want to accept agent buyers are the second payer.
problem: Pix, UPI and M-Pesa are push rails: instantly final, with no chargeback culture. When an agent buys the wrong SKU, gets prompt-injected, or loops, the money is simply gone. Visa and Mastercard still have no binding agent-chargeback rule, and the ledger shows only amount, time and merchant, with no record of why the agent paid. Merchants cannot tell a legitimate agent buyer from an abusive one, and PSPs cannot price the risk.
solution: An API that wraps agent-initiated push payments in a short programmable hold (2-24h) through a licensed partner PSP's escrow or split-payment accounts, or through UPI block-and-debit mandates. Each payment carries a signed 'decision receipt': the user's mandate, a hash of the agent's tool-call trace, price-check evidence and model version. A small human adjudication desk releases or refunds by published rules. PSPs, merchants and insurers all accept the receipt as evidence. The SDK is free; money movement and adjudication are the paid layer.
why_now: Agent rails (AP2 mandates, Mastercard Verifiable Intent, MPP, x402, ACP/UCP) all solve authorization but none define fault or evidence for push rails. India ends zero-MDR UPI for large P2M payments on Oct 15, and a rail that starts charging merchants acquires card-like dispute expectations. Insurers are adding AI exclusions, so they need telemetry to price anything. The Ninth Circuit's 'the agent is the user' ruling pushes liability toward users and their intermediaries.
revenue_model: 0.2-0.4% of held volume, $0.02-0.05 per receipt at scale, and dispute-handling fees paid by whichever side loses. Later, an evidence-pack license to PSPs and insurers underwriting agent risk.
non_obvious_insight: In emerging markets most digital volume rides rails with no chargeback system, so agent error is an unhedged first-class risk there. Whoever holds the neutral, tamper-evident record of why an agent paid becomes the arbiter, and eventually the underwriter, for every party. The cards networks are structurally slow to solve this for rails they do not run.
first_30_days: Publish an open-source decision-receipt SDK for agents that pay via Pix or UPI. Recruit 10 small agent builders (WhatsApp bill-pay and shopping bots) on developer communities. Sign one licensed PSP for escrow sandbox accounts. Hand-adjudicate the first 100 disputes yourselves to learn the fault taxonomy, then price the hold as a paid tier.

title: Designed Toxin Binders for Mouse-Free Antivenom QC
one_liner: Sequence-defined, AI-designed toxin-class binders sold as reference reagents that let antivenom makers test potency without mouse lethality assays.
customer: Antivenom manufacturers (public institutes in Latin America and India, plus private and UK/US firms), WHO and regulator working groups, toxinology labs, and funders such as Wellcome and Gates for later recombinant antivenom.
problem: WHO's 2017 guidelines say murine LD50 and ED50 lethality tests remain the only validated preclinical potency method, despite 3Rs pressure. ELISA, nAChR-binding and cytotoxicity surrogates exist but lack stable, defined, universal reagents, because animal-derived antibodies vary lot to lot.
solution: Produce designed binders for the major toxin families (three-finger toxins, PLA2, SVMP) in E. coli, following the approach in Nature (Jan 2025), where de novo proteins neutralized three-finger toxins and protected mice. Sell (1) calibrator and capture-reagent kits for competition ELISA and nAChR-competition assays, and (2) a 'toxin-family neutralization profile' service showing what each antivenom lot neutralizes, correlated to mouse ED50 over 10-20 lots. Later, co-develop recombinant cocktails.
why_now: The 2025 Nature paper proved designed proteins can neutralize venom toxins. WHO explicitly encourages alternatives. Regulators are moving toward non-animal methods (FDA's Sept 21, 2026 rule is the latest signal). AI design has made binders cheap.
revenue_model: $2-10k research-use kits, $5-20k per lot profile service, grants ($200k-2M) for validation, and later per-dose royalties on recombinant products.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone frames designed antivenom as a therapeutic moonshot. The wedge is quality control: reagents sell before regulators accept a replacement, and manufacturers already pay for mouse colonies. Sequence-defined reagents beat animal-derived ones on reproducibility. Honest caveat: first revenue is likely grants plus small reagent orders.
first_30_days: Check IP with the University of Washington and DTU or design new binders. Express three binders. Send sample sets to 2 antivenom labs for correlation on 10 lots. Apply for a small grant while selling research-use kits to toxinology labs.

title: Fee-Free Hire Receipts for Migrant Workers
one_liner: A worker-held credential proving a migrant was recruited without fees and paid as contracted, sold to suppliers and brands that must prove no forced labour, and portable to the worker's next job.
customer: Tier-1 suppliers and their EU-facing brand buyers in electronics, garments, construction, hospitality and palm oil. Ethical recruitment agencies are a channel, and the worker is the holder.
problem: From 14 December 2027 the EU Forced Labour Regulation bans products made with forced labour, and importers must prove a negative. Audits are sampled snapshots that are easy to game. Workers in corridors such as Nepal to Malaysia or the Philippines to the Gulf often pay illegal recruitment fees that create debt bondage, and they leave with no portable record of employment or skills.
solution: A WhatsApp-first Hire Receipt. At contract signing the worker gets a signed record of recruiter, employer, wage, contract terms and fees paid (zero, or reimbursed). On arrival there is a passport-custody check, then monthly wage-receipt confirmations. Short translated voice check-ins provide independent verification. The worker holds the credential and shares it on consent with employers and brands, which see aggregate dashboards. Over time it accrues employment history and endorsements usable for the next placement or a remittance-backed loan.
why_now: Law firms published compliance roadmaps for the regulation in September 2026, and brands are starting to build supplier evidence programs 15 months before enforcement. Recruitment-fee evidence is the hardest part to get, and no one holds it continuously.
revenue_model: $10-25 per hire paid by the employer or brand, per-site dashboard subscriptions, and placement referral fees from ethical recruiters later.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance buyers must prove a negative, and only worker-side records can do that. Audits fail because they sample, while a worker-held receipt makes evidence continuous, cheaper and self-enforcing. Because the same credential improves the worker's mobility, the worker's incentives align with the buyer's.
first_30_days: Partner with two ethical recruiters in one corridor and one EU-facing supplier. Pilot for 200 hires using a WhatsApp bot rather than an app. Charge a $5k pilot fee plus a per-hire fee, and write up the evidence pack in the format a brand's compliance team will accept.

title: Verified Pay Receipts for Truck Driver Hiring
one_liner: Drivers upload settlement stubs and AI turns them into the true, receipts-backed pay per mile and per hour away from home for every carrier, sold as a hiring credential and as income proof for lenders.
customer: Honest mid-size carriers (50 to 1,000 trucks) that pay $6k to $15k to hire each driver and can't prove their pay claims are real. Secondary buyers are mortgage and auto lenders (bank-statement and non-QM brokers) who serve drivers.
problem: Recruiter ads say 'up to 75 cents a mile, $100k+' but realized pay is often 20 to 35% lower after unpaid or practical-versus-paid miles, unpaid detention, chargebacks and deductions. Driver turnover at big truckload carriers runs near 90%, and job ads are so discredited that honest carriers can't stand out. Drivers whose pay is structured as tax-free 'per diem' also see a low W-2 and get denied mortgages after 20 years of work. Estimates say the English-proficiency and non-domiciled CDL crackdowns will pull 214,000 to 437,000 drivers (5 to 12% of CDL holders) from the supply over 2 to 3 years, so carriers are competing harder for domestic drivers.
solution: A mobile app where drivers photograph settlement stubs and pay statements. AI extracts paid miles, deadhead, detention, deductions, per diem and time away from home, and computes effective take-home per hour on the road, not just per mile. Public carrier pages show verified figures such as '312 verified drivers, median $0.61 per paid mile, $17.40 per hour away'. Carriers that look good pay for a 'Verified Pay' badge and applicant funnel. A second product builds an income-verification packet from stubs and deposit statements for lenders. Fraud controls include stub-format checks, duplicate detection and consistency with driver-reported miles.
why_now: Shrinking driver supply from the 2025 to 2026 English-proficiency out-of-service enforcement (proposed codification rule published Aug 10, 2026) and the Feb 2026 non-domiciled CDL restrictions means cost-per-hire is rising. Vision-model OCR of messy pay stubs is now cheap and accurate. Truth-in-leasing rules already require itemized settlements, so the raw material exists.
revenue_model: Carrier subscriptions of $500 to $3,000 a month for the verified page, analytics and applicant funnel. Lender referral fees of $300 to $1,000 per funded mortgage or truck loan. Free for drivers, which keeps the data supply growing.
non_obvious_insight: Drivers don't compare carriers by ads, they ask in the truck-stop lot 'what do you actually clear?' The only artifact they trust is a pay stub. The honest carriers are the ones locked out of trust, so they are the natural paying customer. The true unit of pay is dollars per hour away from home, because 14-hour clocks, detention and unpaid waiting eat the mileage math. And per-diem income structures are a hidden mortgage trap that a stub-based income packet can fix.
first_30_days: Post in trucker Facebook groups, Reddit and TikTok: 'Upload your stub, see your real rate vs. what your carrier advertised.' Aim for 500 stubs in 30 days. Publish a 'State of Real Pay' report ranking 20 named carriers and pitch it to trade press (Overdrive, CDLLife, FreightWaves). Sell 'Verified Pay' badges to the 5 mid-size fleets whose numbers look best, and sign one bank-statement mortgage broker for lender leads.

title: Public-Records Vault for City Employee AI Chats
one_liner: Capture, retain, redact and produce every government employee's AI prompt and response as the public record it legally is.
customer: City clerks, county records officers and city attorneys at cities of 20-300K people that just rolled out AI assistants to staff.
problem: Every prompt and output from a government employee is likely a public record subject to retention schedules and open-records requests. Cities are turning AI on in Chattanooga-style rollouts with no retention system. A single request from a journalist could force manual digging through vendor logs the city may not control.
solution: Browser extension and API proxy that captures AI interactions across tools, tags them to retention schedules, redacts exempt content (personnel, law enforcement, attorney-client), and generates one-click productions for open-records requests. Litigation-hold support included.
why_now: Local AI adoption is now real, with police, school and bus-routing deployments. GenAI.mil users have built more than 100k agents. Records lawyers are starting to warn, and the first open-records fights over chatbot logs will land in 2026-27.
revenue_model: $8-40K per year per city by headcount, plus e-discovery production fees. Reseller channel via records-management vendors.
non_obvious_insight: AI adoption creates a records problem before it creates a safety problem. The clerk, not the CIO, has a legal deadline and a small budget line for exactly this.
first_30_days: Talk to 10 city clerks and 3 state records associations. Build the capture extension for two chat tools and a retention-schedule mapper. Pilot free with 2 cities that have announced AI programs, and convert on the first open-records request.

title: Second Look: Illustrators as Fake-Image Examiners
one_liner: A bench of displaced illustrators and retouchers trained as human image examiners who certify or flag photos in insurance claims, rental deposits, and e-commerce refunds, with written, defensible reasons.
customer: Small and mid P&C insurers, MGAs and third-party administrators, warranty and protection-plan providers, short-term-rental platforms and property managers, and marketplace trust-and-safety teams. $6-30 per reviewed image set or $2-6k/month retainers.
problem: A March 2026 Verisk study found 98% of insurers agree AI editing is fueling digital fraud and 99% have seen manipulated documentation. Only 7% of anti-fraud professionals rated their orgs more than moderately prepared. Detection software returns probabilities, not explanations, and subtle 'vanilla synthetic' edits (a crack added to a countertop) fool adjusters. A claims team can't deny a claim or testify on a '78% AI' score.
solution: A trained reviewer network that triages with detection software, then writes structured, defensible rationales a special investigations unit can use in denials or disputes ('shadow direction contradicts the window; wood grain repeats; crack terminus violates stress geometry'). Reviewers train on a continuously refreshed library of fakes. Reports are usable in SIU files. A 'fake gym' subscription trains in-house adjusters.
why_now: Insurers' alarm about AI-generated claim images is documented in 2026 (Debevoise, SAS, Verisk). Watermarking and labeling rules like the EU AI Act's Article 50 (effective August 2026) bind good-faith providers, while fraudsters use tools that don't mark outputs or strip metadata. Illustrators are among the most displaced creative workers.
revenue_model: Per-image and per-claim fees, monthly retainers, $150-300 expert-report add-ons, training subscriptions, and a white-label human tier for detection vendors.
non_obvious_insight: The best detector of a fake image is a person who could have made it. Fake-spotting is a craft-knowledge problem about why light, material, and structure cannot be that way, and illustrators hold the largest pool of exactly that knowledge. What insurers need is an explanation they can defend, not a probability.
first_30_days: Build a 200-image benchmark of real versus AI-edited damage photos and publish humans-versus-tools accuracy. Recruit 8 illustrators from artist communities. Pitch 3 MGAs or TPAs and one rental-property manager. Offer a paid pilot at about $10 per claim and close the first one within 60 days.

title: Warranty Clock Recovery Audits for Idle Halls
one_liner: A contingency-fee service that finds and files the warranty claims on energized-but-empty data halls before OEM warranty clocks silently expire.
customer: Colocation developers, powered-shell landlords, neocloud operators and enterprise owners with phased or delayed-tenant builds, especially those with halls commissioned 6-14 months ago and not yet loaded. The owner pays a percentage of recovered value, plus an optional per-asset tracking subscription.
problem: Warranty clocks on generators, UPS systems, chillers, CRAH/CDUs, switchgear, and batteries usually start at shipment or startup, not when a tenant loads the hall. With delayed leases and mid-build AI redesigns, halls sit energized and idle for months. Many defects only show under real load (UPS capacitors, chiller compressors, wet-stacking gensets, breaker trip curves, coolant chemistry). By the time the tenant ramps, the warranty has expired. The turnover package is 50,000+ pages of PDFs that ops never reads, the punch-list deferrals are lost, and OEM maintenance records required to keep coverage valid are often missing. Nobody owns the clock.
solution: Ingest POs, OEM warranty terms, startup sheets, Cx reports, shipping documents and maintenance logs with an LLM pipeline to build a serial-number-level warranty ledger with real expiry dates and voiding conditions. Flag anything expiring within 120 days. Run a targeted load-dependent-defect inspection before expiry (thermography, oil and coolant samples, capacitor and battery checks, breaker testing). File claims, negotiate warranty start-date deferrals or extensions with the OEM while leverage still exists, and fix missing maintenance-record gaps. For new builds, sell a PO-stage clause pack that defers warranty start to beneficial occupancy.
why_now: There is a glut of speculative shells and delayed tenant handoffs. Reporting in 2026 shows close to half of planned US builds slipping, with only about a third of 2026 target capacity under active construction. That means many halls are powered, commissioned and idle. Equipment was bought at peak prices with tariffs on steel, aluminum and copper, so each lapsed warranty is worth more. LLMs can now read messy closeout binders cheaply, which was the labor bottleneck for audits like this.
revenue_model: 25-30% of recovered value or avoided cost on claims and negotiated extensions, no fee if nothing is recovered. Optional $150-400 per asset per year tracking subscription. $15K-40K fixed-fee closeout audits for owners who want certainty. PO-stage clause-pack consulting for developers.
non_obvious_insight: The warranty is the only major asset on a data center balance sheet that expires silently. OEMs will defer warranty start dates at PO time, but almost no one negotiates it because the project team is fighting for delivery slots, not paperwork. After the fact, the owner's ops team inherits the docs with no idea when the clocks started. The money is in the punch-list items that were 'to be fixed later' and the load-dependent defects that only appear after the hall is finally used.
first_30_days: Find 3 owner-operators through PM and Cx network contacts with halls energized 8-11 months ago and not fully loaded. Offer a free 10-day scan of their closeout binders in exchange for a contingency agreement on any claims. Build the extraction pipeline on real binders (gensets, UPS, chillers first). Deliver a 'expiring within 90 days' hit list and file the first claims before the first invoice.

title: Bot-Proof Local Comments: Verified Neighbors, Pseudonymous
one_liner: Secret and Yik Yak died of unaccountable anonymity and Digg's March 2026 relaunch died of bots; the missing primitive is 'one real human, from this place, no real name', and local newsrooms and city councils will pay for it.
customer: Independent and nonprofit local newsrooms (hundreds exist) that have switched off comments, and city, county and school-board clerks running public comment for hearings on rezonings, data centers and levies.
problem: Newsrooms disabled comment sections because of toxicity and bots, so local conversation moved to Facebook groups. Public bodies get astroturf and AI-generated comment floods (the 2017 FCC net-neutrality docket was later found mostly fake by New York's attorney general) and cannot tell residents from out-of-area campaigns or bots.
solution: An embeddable comment and public-comment widget. Each person verifies once via a state mobile ID in Apple or Google Wallet with address check, or a postcard PIN or voter-file match as fallback, then posts under a pseudonym. The platform attests only 'verified human, resident of ZIP or ward X'. Public bodies get a verified-resident tally (for example, '412 verified residents commented, 78% opposed, 61 from Ward 3'). One credential works across the paper, council and school board, and publishers never see identity.
why_now: Digg's open beta launched 14 January 2026 and shut on 14 March 2026 after bot and AI-agent floods. Agents can now write plausible public comments at scale. Mobile IDs in phone wallets make cheap, high-assurance verification possible. Local news funders are paying for audience-trust infrastructure.
revenue_model: $200-1,500/mo per newsroom; $500-3,000/mo per municipality or agency for a verified public-comment portal; per-verification fees ($0.50-1.50) sponsored by foundations or civic funders; later, verified local polling panels.
non_obvious_insight: Anonymity was never the fatal flaw; unverifiable anonymity was. In a bot-saturated internet, 'provably a real neighbor' becomes the scarce good, and local institutions already need it but cannot buy it. The credential also compounds: a resident verified once for the newspaper is reusable for council, school board and library levy comments.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 small newsrooms through nonprofit-news networks to run a verified-comment pilot on one hot local issue (rezoning or data center) using SMS or postcard plus voter-file match. Publish the verified-tally story, then pitch the same town's clerk a public-comment pilot. Charge $250/mo after the pilot.

title: ARIA Watch: Aide Eyes for Alzheimer's Drug Clinics
one_liner: A 60-second daily safety check done by the home aide or family for patients on anti-amyloid drugs, flagging the subtle change that precedes brain-swelling side effects, sold to the memory clinic that prescribes them.
customer: Neurology and memory practices and infusion or injection programs running Leqembi and Kisunla. The buyer is the practice manager or program nurse coordinator. The revenue partner is the patient's home care agency.
problem: Anti-amyloid drugs carry ARIA (brain swelling or bleeding) risk, mostly caught by MRI at scheduled points. Symptoms such as headache, dizziness, vision change, new confusion or seizures often appear between scans. A person with dementia cannot report them. The infusion nurse sees the patient for two hours every two weeks and cannot judge baseline. The person who can is the aide, who sees the patient every morning and says 'she's not herself today.' Nobody asks the aide.
solution: A structured, plain-language daily check on a phone, with a voice option in the aide's language. It records a few observations against the patient's own baseline: gait, speech, new headache behavior, appetite, alertness and a free-text 'not herself'. A protocol turns 'change from baseline' into three levels: log, call the nurse today, or send to the ED. Alerts land in the clinic's inbox with a timeline. Aides get a small per-check stipend. The agency gets a revenue share. The practice gets documentation for safety programs and the patient-family peace of mind that keeps them on therapy.
why_now: The FDA approved Leqembi Iqlik, a home-administered subcutaneous starting dose, in July 2026, with launch in late August. Fewer infusion visits means fewer clinician touchpoints, while MRI-based ARIA monitoring remains. FDA-cleared blood tests are increasing the number of treated patients. CMS finalized new 2026 remote-monitoring codes for 2-15 days of data (99445) and the first 10 minutes of management (99470), making light-touch programs billable. Self-reported observations alone do not qualify for RPM, so the model pairs with a connected BP or pulse-ox device or bills through care-management routes such as CCM, PCM or GUIDE.
revenue_model: $45-65 per patient per month paid by the practice. A $10-15 per month stipend to the aide or agency comes out of that. Optional device add-on to unlock RPM billing. Later, pharma-funded real-world safety and function studies drawn from the aide-observed baseline data.
non_obvious_insight: The most valuable clinical sensor for a patient who cannot self-report is the person who changes their sheets. Aide phrasing like 'not herself' or 'slower' is a better early signal than a symptom checklist the patient can't complete, and it arrives as a behavior change, not a complaint. Home care agencies have always been treated as a cost center by clinics. Here they become a data channel that clinics will pay for.
first_30_days: Talk to 10 memory clinic nurse coordinators and two infusion-center managers and ask what they do between MRIs. Build the check as a no-login web form and SMS. Recruit 3 agencies whose clients are on Leqembi or Kisunla, plus a neurologist champion. Offer a free 90-day pilot on 15 patients, with a monthly report of flags raised and calls avoided. Convert to per-patient pricing once one true early catch is documented.

title: Compliance Rail for Verified Bio-AI Labs
one_liner: A 'SOC 2 for AI-directed biology': fast dossiers plus continuous evidence collection that let small labs qualify for, and keep, verified access to frontier bio-AI.
customer: Small biotechs, CROs, academic cores and AI-bio startups applying to verification programs (Anthropic expects hundreds of organizations in week one); later insurers and pharma partners that request attestations.
problem: Trend chain: frontier providers now gate relaxed bio safeguards behind credential, security and ethics-oversight review. Next, each provider and government runs a slightly different program. Then small labs discover they lack security staff, an oversight committee, or records separating AI proposal, human edit and robot execution (a gap Lab Manager flags, since CDC and WHO frameworks predate autonomous systems). Each application becomes bespoke paperwork.
solution: Week 1: a 5-day 'verification-ready' dossier covering security-control mapping (SOC 2 and ISO 27001-lite), personnel credential packet, data-retention and access configuration, and a dual-use risk register. Optionally add a rent-an-oversight-committee: an independent biosafety and dual-use review board with documented minutes. Month 3 onward: connectors to ELN, LIMS, robot logs and AI-provider logs produce an audit trail and a portable attestation that is reused across providers.
why_now: Anthropic's Life Sciences Verification Program launched Sept 17, 2026, with 30-day data retention and 'hundreds of organizations' expected in the first week. Other providers are likely to follow (an inference). Autonomous labs are multiplying with no accountability standard.
revenue_model: $3-8k per dossier, $1.5-4k/month for oversight-committee and evidence subscription, and per-attestation fees from providers or insurers.
non_obvious_insight: Relaxed safeguards become a competitive credential the way SOC 2 became table stakes in SaaS. The bottleneck is not the AI provider's review but small organizations' inability to package proof. Once two or more providers run programs, a portable attestation beats bespoke applications, and the evidence stream also feeds insurers.
first_30_days: Turn the public criteria into a 40-point readiness checklist. Sell a $1.5k readiness review to 20 startups via SynBioBeta and LinkedIn. Partner with an IBC or biosafety consultancy for the oversight-committee product. Ship the dossier template.

title: Flood Closing Desk for Title Agents
one_liner: A day-one flood file on every purchase: elevation, zone challenge, private flood substitute and NFIP-lapse fallback.
customer: Title and escrow agencies and mortgage brokers in coastal and riverine markets, with contingency fees from homeowners.
problem: NFIP authority expires Sept 30 2026 after more than 30 short-term extensions. In the 2010 lapse about 1,400 closings a day were delayed or cancelled (secondary source). Even without a lapse, zone and elevation problems surface on day 25 of a 30-day contract, and premiums must roughly double toward full risk.
solution: An order-time 'Flood File': LiDAR-derived elevation, zone confirmation, candidates for a Letter of Map Amendment, an instant private-flood quote with a compliance letter as an NFIP substitute during lapses, and a Risk Rating 2.0 estimate. Title agencies embed it in their order flow.
why_now: Authority lapses in two days, and premium glide-path increases make every flood file a live cost.
revenue_model: $95-250 per file, $500-1,500 contingency for successful zone removal, and private flood placement commission.
non_obvious_insight: Buyers and lenders pay to avoid closing delays. Zone challenges are an arbitrage, since a successful removal saves the owner premiums every year.
first_30_days: Contract with 5 title offices, partner with a surveyor, hand-deliver 100 files, and track removal success rates.

title: Hype-Item Triage for Thrift and Charity Shops
one_liner: A 10-second back-room scan station that tells thrift and charity staff which donated sneakers and collectibles are worth $150 instead of $12, then lists them online for a revenue share.
customer: Independent Goodwill regionals, church and charity thrift shops, Plato's Closet-style franchisees, consignment shops and estate-sale companies. They pay a rev share on the uplift, or $199 per month per store.
problem: Thrift pricers are paid to move volume and price shoes at a flat $8 to $25 by category. Meanwhile teen and adult resellers ('pickers') walk the racks right after restock and buy the $12 pairs worth $200 and up. Donations are the shop's raw material, and the shop is giving the profit to the pickers. Charities lose real money, and staff cannot read a style code or tell a real pair from a fake, so they either underprice or avoid the risk.
solution: A tablet at the sorting table. Staff photograph the tongue tag or box label. OCR pulls the style code and size, then the app returns resale value, days-to-sell, condition-adjusted price and known fake tells for that model. Anything over $60 goes into an 'online' bin. Our remote team of college and teen resellers lists, ships and remits the shop's share, so the shop needs no e-commerce staff. Later categories: trading cards, LEGO, vintage tees, Stanley cups, Pokemon sealed product, watches.
why_now: Thrift has boomed with Gen Z while tariffs push shoppers to secondhand, which also means more pickers hitting the same racks. Multimodal models now read tag photos accurately and cheaply. Donations arrive in volume, but shop margins are squeezed by picker competition and labor costs. Charities have never had a hype-specific tool.
revenue_model: 20% to 30% of net sale price on items routed to online, or a SaaS fee per store. Charities are motivated because it is found money for their programs.
non_obvious_insight: The biggest sneaker sourcing channel for resellers is a flat-price system that cannot see value. The knowledge needed is tiny: style code, size, box, one authenticity tell. That is why resellers win, and it can be sold to the seller side. Being reseller-native gives me trust with staff and the sourcing instincts to know which categories are next.
first_30_days: Offer three local charity thrift shops a free two-week pilot. I sort through their back room on a Saturday, list the top 30 items, and split proceeds with the charity (charity 70%, us 30%). Track the uplift versus what those items would have sold for on the floor. Turn the numbers into a one-page case study and pitch 20 more independent thrift operators.

title: Hazmat Sidecar for Small Old-House Repairs
one_liner: A flat-price, same-week asbestos and lead test-and-remove service that solo-to-five-tech plumbing, HVAC, electrical and flooring shops call when a small job in a pre-1980 house hits suspect material, with the waste manifest handled for them.
customer: Small trade shops (pay per call and pass through) and homeowners; property managers are a later segment.
problem: Median home age is 44 years and 62% of homeowners now choose repair over replace, so small jobs constantly disturb duct wrap, vinyl tile, transite, plaster and lead paint. Licensed abatement firms impose $2-5K minimums and weeks of lead time, so contractors either walk away (feeding the 73% project backlog) or cut corners and carry liability. Few landfills accept asbestos waste, and manifests and pre-notification confuse small shops.
solution: A van with two accredited techs: same-week sample results through a partner lab, flat-fee minor removal where state rules allow (subcontracted where they don't), bagged, labeled and manifested disposal, and a digital clearance letter the trade can hand the homeowner. Shops book by text and can subscribe for priority.
why_now: Repair-over-replace, tariff-inflated equipment and HVAC's 2025 shipment trough leave small shops chasing any billable job and unwilling to lose one to a hazmat surprise. Larger platforms (ServiceTitan, PE roll-ups) do not serve sub-$10K jobs.
revenue_model: $300-1,500 per job; per-sample testing fees; $99/mo priority subscription for trade shops.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not removal labor but the disposal chain: manifests, landfill acceptance and pollution insurance. Owning that chain lets one small team become the referral default for every trade in the area.
first_30_days: Days 1-30: complete state inspector accreditation, lead-safe firm certification and worker courses, get a pollution-liability quote and sign a landfill acceptance agreement. Meanwhile pre-sign 10 trade shops to a flat-price menu. Days 30-90: run the first 20 jobs and refine pricing.

title: Cloud Machine Shop for High-School Shop Class
one_liner: Students design parts, watch real CNC machines cut them live at a partner job shop, and receive the parts by mail, so any school gets a hands-on manufacturing lab without machines or instructors.
customer: High-school and community-college CTE and robotics programs (per-project fees, often funded by CTE grants); job shops sponsor for recruiting.
problem: Manufacturing has openings, but CNC labs cost $100k+ and need instructors who are scarce, so rural and small schools cannot offer them. AI can now generate designs but students never touch real machining. Hands-on work is also the AI-resilient part of learning.
solution: A web portal: design in browser CAD with AI assist, automatic manufacturability checks and CAM by the partner shop, a scheduled live-stream slot where the machine cuts the student's part with a shop mentor narrating, then shipment. Curriculum aligns to entry-level machining credential levels and gives teachers a dashboard.
why_now: Text-to-CAD and instant-quote manufacturing platforms are good enough in 2026, streaming is trivial, and job shops have idle off-peak capacity and hiring pain. School AI pauses and screen fatigue make hands-on offerings attractive.
revenue_model: $25-60 per student project, $3-6k per classroom per year, plus recruiting sponsorship from job shops and manufacturer associations.
non_obvious_insight: Equipment and instructors are the constraint, not student interest. Machines already run from files, so the lab can be teleported, and idle night-shift capacity is a free asset that the shop's hiring pain will pay to use.
first_30_days: Partner with one local job shop with a couple of machines available off-peak. Recruit 5 CTE or robotics teachers. Run a 3-week design-and-cut unit at $30 per student and measure engagement. Map the unit to a machining credential standard.

title: Cinemas and Arcades as Paid Heat Refuges
one_liner: A standby network of independent cinemas, bowling alleys, arcades and LAN centers that counties activate on heat and smoke days and pay per verified visit.
customer: County and city heat or emergency-management offices, starting with one that has a heat-action plan and a live indoor-temperature mandate (LA County, Maryland counties). Landlords of buildings under indoor temperature caps are the second buyer.
problem: Cooling centers are libraries and rec centers with short hours. Seniors, night-shift workers and teens do not go. Cooling is now a legal duty for landlords: Maryland 80F cap since June 2026, LA County 82F from Jan 2027, NYC 78F from 2030 (secondary sources). When a chiller fails, the fallback is hotel rooms at $150+ a night. Meanwhile independent cinemas, bowling alleys and family entertainment centers sit half-empty on weekday afternoons, with HVAC sized for 300 people.
solution: Pre-contract 20-60 venues per county under a standby agreement. A heat trigger (heat index or WBGT threshold) or smoke trigger (AQI above 150) activates them. On activation, venues open a free-entry lane with water, a screening and a quiet room. Outreach goes out by 211, SMS and health-plan lists, and QR or phone check-in creates per-visit proof. The county pays a standby fee plus a per-verified-visit-hour fee. Landlords can buy prepaid outage passes for tenants when their cooling fails.
why_now: Summer 2026 was reported as the hottest US July on record, and the European heatwave death toll shifted political attention. Cooling mandates are arriving on a 2027-2032 phase-in, so demand is scheduled, not random. FEMA's BRIC money was cancelled, court-restored and then closed to applications on Jul 23 2026, so cities need cheap opex solutions rather than built capacity. Venues want non-ticket revenue.
revenue_model: $150-400 standby fee per venue per heat season, plus $8-15 per verified visit-hour paid by the county. The platform keeps about 25%. Landlord outage passes at $10-15 per tenant-day. Venues keep concession sales.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce thing in a heat emergency is not cold air. It is willingness to go somewhere and stay for six hours. Entertainment venues are dwell-time machines that already hold 300 people at 70F with a reason to stay. Paying only for activated days flips cooling centers from capex to opex with zero idle capacity, and smoke days come free because cinemas can run high-grade filtration.
first_30_days: Pick one county with a heat-action plan and a 2027 budget cycle. Sign LOIs from 5-8 owner-operated cinemas, bowling alleys and arcade bars (phone calls, not enterprise sales). Run an unpaid test activation on the next warm spell or smoke day. Write a one-page cost comparison against hotel vouchers and take it to the county emergency office, one Medicaid managed-care plan and 10 property managers.

title: Section 8 Rent-Increase Deadline Capture Service
one_liner: A tracker that knows each voucher tenant's lease anniversary, sees the new FY2027 payment standard, and files the landlord's rent-increase request inside the tight 60-day window before a year of raise is forfeited.
customer: Small landlords with 1 to 50 Housing Choice Voucher units, especially out-of-state investors in Section 8-heavy markets such as Memphis, Cleveland, St. Louis and Indianapolis. Small PM firms with voucher portfolios are the second segment.
problem: Housing-authority payment standards rose for FY2027, but a new standard does not flow through to an existing tenancy on October 1. It applies only at each tenant's lease anniversary. The owner must send a written request within a typically tight window, often 60 days before that date, or forfeit the increase for a year. Each housing authority has its own forms and dates. Most small owners never map the anniversary dates, so they leave real money uncollected. One market analysis found 3-bedroom increases of 6 to 12%, with a median of 10%.
solution: The landlord uploads photos of their HAP contracts and leases, and the tool extracts tenant anniversary dates and current contract rents. The team maintains a database of housing-authority payment standards and each authority's request process (scraped from PHA PDFs and notices, human-verified). For each unit it computes the increase headroom, alerts at 90, 75 and 60 days before the window closes, and generates the authority-specific rent-increase request letter or form. It tracks proof of submission and logs who was contacted and when. It also flags likely mistakes in the original rent-reasonableness record (wrong bedroom count or square footage) that justify a correction request mid-lease.
why_now: FY2027 standards take effect around October 1, 2026, and today is 2026-09-28. Anniversary windows are opening across the country right now. The forum thread on this appeared within days, and the one-year forfeiture is a hard deadline that makes people spend money.
revenue_model: Success-aligned pricing: $5 per unit per month, plus 1 month of the captured increase for each unit where the request is approved. On a $1,300 rent and a 10% bump, that is $130 per month, or $1,560 a year, per unit. Authority data is the moat; a PM-firm plan can charge per door. Later, a similar deadline tracker can cover annual recertification and inspection dates.
non_obvious_insight: The money is lost to a calendar, not to the tenant or the market, and the people who feel it are the least likely to be organized. A BiggerPockets post titled 'Section 8 rents went up for FY2027. Most landlords won't collect it' says: 'A new payment standard does not flow through to an existing tenancy on October 1'. It adds that owners must submit written requests within a typically tight 60-day window before each anniversary or forfeit the opportunity for an entire year. It reports 3-bedroom rates up 6-12% (median 10%) in nine of ten low-cost ZIP codes, and notes that St. Louis adopted its FY2027 standards effective Jan 1, 2027 (https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/52/topics/1301792-section-8-rents-went-up-for-fy2027-most-landlords-wont-collect-it). Out-of-state voucher landlords also struggle with local rules, as in a Cleveland thread on Section 8 inspection standards (https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/963/topics/1302305-furnace-and-water-heater-on-wood-platforms-cleveland-section-8-inspection). A separate thread notes Section 8 tenants are 'already at maximum allowable rates' (https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/963/topics/1302138-how-realistic-is-it-to-raise-rents-100-on-existing-tenants).
first_30_days: Week 1: hand-build payment-standard tables and request procedures for 3 housing authorities (start with St. Louis, Cleveland and Memphis). Publish a free calculator, 'How much did you leave on the table this year?', in the BiggerPockets Out-of-State and Landlording forums. Weeks 2 to 3: onboard 15 landlords, send requests manually with the templates, and track approvals. Week 4: turn on success-fee billing, and pitch 3 small voucher-heavy PM firms. Target: 15 landlords, 100+ units, and 10 documented approved increases.

title: Common Rooms: Community-Share Buyouts of Neighborhood Bars
one_liner: A studio that helps retiring owners sell beloved bars, cafes, bookstores and cinemas to hundreds of neighbors through community-share offers, then supplies a manager and shared back office.
customer: Owners over 60 of profitable independent third-place businesses who can't find a buyer, plus neighbors who buy $100-500 shares. Commercial landlords are a third stakeholder.
problem: Boomers own most main-street businesses and many will simply close, because a qualified buyer with SBA-loan credit is rare. Communities lose their remaining third places while loneliness is a public-health issue.
solution: The UK community-pub playbook, using US tools: a Reg CF offering (up to $5M a year), an LLC or co-op with member voting, a pre-launch pledge drive to prove 300-800 neighbor investors, a professional general manager, and a shared back office (bookkeeping, permits, POS, purchasing) across all venues in the portfolio. Community shares replace acquisition debt so the business isn't forced to service a loan.
why_now: Peak-65 owners are exiting in volume, Reg CF and its platforms are mature, and retail vacancy plus loneliness make the case politically easy. In the UK, community pubs have raised about GBP 35M from 37,500+ shareholders, but the US has no equivalent operator.
revenue_model: Success fee of 3-5% of the raise, a monthly management-services contract ($1.5-3k) per venue, and vendor rebates from pooled purchasing.
non_obvious_insight: Community ownership doesn't sell returns, it sells guaranteed regulars. 500 shareholders who each show up twice a month are a customer base that exists before the doors reopen, and that is why these businesses survive at much higher rates than buyer-owned ones. The moat is the repeatable legal and marketing kit and the shared back office, not any single deal.
first_30_days: Choose one metro and phone 25 owners over 60. Find three with positive cash flow willing to sell at roughly 2-3x seller's discretionary earnings. Launch a pledge page ('would you put $250 into saving X?') to prove demand, and retain securities counsel for a templated Reg CF filing. Charge a small engagement fee up front, with the balance due on close.

title: Forever Guardian: Lifetime Care After Parents Are Gone
one_liner: A prepaid, life-insurance-funded successor-care plan in which a named team becomes the lifelong advocate, money manager and care coordinator for an adult with a disability after the parents are gone.
customer: Parents in their 60s-80s of adult children with intellectual or developmental disabilities (nearly one million US households have adults with I/DD living with an aging caregiver). Referred by special-needs planning attorneys and financial planners.
problem: Parents dread 'who will look after them when we're gone.' Siblings are often unavailable, state Medicaid waiver waitlists are long, pooled special-needs trusts manage money but rarely relationships, and no single accountable person exists for decades. The current autism generation is about to become adults, and the adult cohort will surge.
solution: A tiered plan. (1) While parents are alive: a named care manager, annual home visit, a living 'letter of intent' binder (routines, medications, preferences), and monthly check-in calls, so the person already knows the successor. (2) At transition: the team acts as advocate or guardian-of-record where allowed, coordinates services, audits group-home quality, and works with a partner trust company holding a pooled special-needs trust. (3) Funded by a paid-up second-to-die life policy or an upfront fee plus a monthly retainer.
why_now: Peak-65 parents are hitting the age where the successor question is urgent, Medicaid home- and community-based services are under financial pressure, and adults with I/DD are living longer than any prior generation. It is a large, emotionally urgent market with no scaled, for-profit successor-care provider.
revenue_model: Upfront enrollment ($5-15k or insurance-funded), a monthly care-management retainer ($100-200), trust administration fees through the partner, and insurance commissions.
non_obvious_insight: The real product is a relationship that starts before the parents die. The annual home visit is both the moat and the sales funnel: by the time a parent passes, the guardian is already someone the adult knows and trusts. It converts a frightening legal product into a service with visible value every month while the parents are still alive to judge it.
first_30_days: Partner with three special-needs planning attorneys and one trust company. Sign 15 families to a $1,500 'Shadow Year' (assessment, letter-of-intent binder, quarterly visits, monthly calls). Hire one care manager and validate the guardianship, trust and licensing requirements for a single state before promising the full lifetime plan.

title: Live Doom-Pile Sessions for Avoided Paperwork
one_liner: A scheduled video session where a calm, admin-savvy host sits with you while you open the unopened mail pile, triages it, and gets the scary items handled before you hang up.
customer: Adults 25-55 with ADHD, anxiety, depression, recent bereavement or new-parent overload pay $59 per session or $89 a month for two sessions. Employer benefit programs, credit unions and probate attorneys pay for seats.
problem: Millions of people leave envelopes and portal notifications unopened because not knowing is more comfortable than knowing. Late fees, collections, missed renewals and tax notices escalate. The avoidance is emotional, so productivity apps and reminder tools do not touch it.
solution: A 45-minute weekly 'Admin Sunday' session. Members upload photos of the pile beforehand and AI produces a triage card (ignore, do this month, act by Friday). A trained host, such as a former paralegal, bookkeeper or benefits caseworker, sits with the member on camera as each envelope is opened. Three actions get done in the session, such as calling with a script, setting up a payment plan, or filing a form. The member leaves with a 'Nothing Scary' summary. A mail-forwarding tier serves people who cannot face even the session.
why_now: Adult ADHD diagnoses have surged and body-doubling is mainstream on TikTok and in tools like Focusmate. LLMs make triage and drafting nearly free, so one human can run 6-8 sessions a day and the business keeps a healthy margin. Collections on federal student loans restarted in 2025, raising the stakes of ignored mail. Consumers now value human presence precisely because AI can read the letter but cannot sit next to you.
revenue_model: $89 monthly subscription for two sessions, $59 a la carte. Hosts are paid $28-35 an hour, giving roughly 55-60% gross margin. B2B seats at $12-20 per employee per month for EAP and financial-wellness buyers.
non_obvious_insight: The product is courage with a witness, not productivity. People will pay to discover bad news in the company of someone calm. Silent co-working apps do not solve this because the body double is not allowed to help, and AI alone cannot absorb the emotion of opening the envelope.
first_30_days: Post in ADHD and adulting communities and make short 'doom pile' videos. Run 10 free consented live sessions to create content and testimonials. Sell $49 founding-member sessions through Stripe and run on Zoom and Google Drive. Recruit 5 hosts from retired paralegal and bookkeeper groups. Goal: 15 paying subscribers by day 30 and 30 by day 60.
